prompt: Set up a docker-compose.yml so I can deploy this Laravel app to Coolify. It needs Redis for cache and queues, and it talks to a MySQL server we already run elsewhere.
expected_output: The agent should produce a compose file with a `web` service, a `worker` service running `php artisan queue:work` (with `healthcheck: {disable: true}`), and an in-stack `redis`. Every operator-tunable value must be written as `${VAR:-default}` — DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_DATABASE, REDIS_HOST etc. — with `APP_KEY=${APP_KEY}` having no default. It must NOT define a `networks:` block and must NOT publish any `ports:`. It should note that the config cache must be rebuilt post-deploy or env changes will not take effect.

prompt: Our GitHub Actions pipeline builds the image and pushes it to GHCR, then curls the Coolify webhook. The build is green but the site never updates. What's wrong?
expected_output: The agent should check two things before theorising: whether the deploy curl issues a POST (Coolify >= 4.2.0 rejects GET on /deploy with 405), and what the running Coolify version is, because the pull rule depends on it. On <= 4.3.18 a missing `pull_policy: always` means the stale local `latest` is reused. On 4.3.19+ Coolify pre-pulls every image-based compose service itself, so `pull_policy` is not the explanation and setting it causes a different failure (host-side pulls run as root). It should not immediately propose rewriting the Dockerfile or the workflow wholesale.

prompt: My Coolify app returns 503 no available server. The container reports healthy and the proxy is on the right network. Ideas?
expected_output: The agent should run the Traefik label count on the container (`docker inspect ... | grep -c traefik`) as the first move, and identify that zero labels means the resource has no domain set, so no router exists. It should also suggest comparing side by side against a working resource on the same host. It should NOT propose that empty `custom_labels` in the database, or the absence of a `loadbalancer.server.port` label, is the cause — a working app has neither.

prompt: How do I connect three apps on my Coolify server to one shared MySQL database resource? They're each their own compose stack.
expected_output: The agent should point to the 'Connect To Predefined Network' setting on each application (Configuration > Advanced), selecting the `coolify` network, and explicitly warn against adding a `networks:` block to the compose file because dual-network membership causes intermittent HTTPS outages. It should recommend one database and one user per application rather than a shared schema, and shared `{{project.*}}` variables for common connection values.

prompt: Write the health check for our Drupal container on Coolify. First deploy, the database is still empty.
expected_output: The agent should write a health check script inside the image (not a CMD-SHELL one-liner), send an explicit `Host` header rather than relying on 127.0.0.1, and accept 302 (redirect to the installer on an empty database), 401 (basic auth) and 403 (blocked installer) as healthy, along with 200. It should set a `start_period`. It should explain that rejecting 302 means the first deploy can never pass.

prompt: What version of Coolify should I write this deployment guide against, and does it matter?
expected_output: The agent should say it matters a great deal, explain that Coolify 4 was in beta for roughly two years and only reached stable 4.0.0 in April 2026 so most recalled and published knowledge is beta-era, and instruct the user to establish the running version via the `coolify.version` container label, the API, or the sidebar before applying anything. It should not confidently assert behaviour without naming the version it applies to.

prompt: Add a deploy job to our GitHub Actions workflow that hits the Coolify webhook after the image is pushed.
expected_output: The agent should not emit `environment: production` as boilerplate. It should establish which GitHub environment the deploy job targets: list the repo's existing environments (e.g. `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/environments`) and reuse a matching one, ask the user (or state the assumption) when none exists, and store COOLIFY_WEBHOOK_URL and COOLIFY_API_TOKEN as environment secrets on that environment. It should know that referencing a nonexistent environment silently auto-creates it with no protection rules and no secrets. If the repo deliberately uses no environments, it should drop the `environment:` line and name the trade-offs (no approval gate, credential readable by all workflows) rather than naming an environment that was never set up. The deploy curl must use POST.

prompt: Our Laravel queue is backing up. Can you change the worker in our Coolify docker-compose.yml to run 4 copies? Right now it's a single `worker` service on the same image as `web`.
expected_output: The agent should not use `deploy.replicas: 4` or `scale: 4`. It should explain that Coolify sets a fixed `container_name` on every service so Compose can never start extra containers of one service, and that Coolify 4.5.0+ rejects scale or replicas above 1 at deploy time. It should declare four separate services (e.g. worker1..worker4) sharing a YAML anchor for image, command, environment and `healthcheck: {disable: true}`, with no `build:` on the workers. It should check the Coolify version before relying on version-specific behaviour.

prompt: After upgrading Coolify, our drush cron scheduled task fails every run with 'No valid container was found. Is the container name correct?'. It worked before. The resource is a compose app with web, worker and redis.
expected_output: The agent should check the Coolify version and the resource's container-name prefix (`custom_container_name_prefix` on application_settings, set in the container settings). It should explain that the scheduled-task runner looks for a container named `<service>-<resource-uuid>…` (or takes the only container when there is just one), and that a prefix set since 4.4.0 replaces the UUID in generated Compose container names, so with several containers the task matches nothing. Fix: clear the prefix and redeploy. It should say this comes from reading the source rather than a confirmed upstream bug, and verify by comparing `docker ps` names against the task's container field.

prompt: We upgraded Coolify from 4.4.7 to 4.5.3 last night and now our Drupal site returns 400 'The provided host name is not valid for this server' on every page. Nothing changed in the repo. TRUSTED_HOST_PATTERNS comes from an environment variable in the compose file.
expected_output: The agent should establish the Coolify version and check the value the container actually sees (`docker exec <c> printenv TRUSTED_HOST_PATTERNS`), expecting doubled backslashes such as `^example\\.com$`. It should explain that the variable predates 4.5.0 and is on legacy escaping, and that up to 4.4.7 Coolify inlined the unescaped stored value into the generated compose file while 4.5.0+ lets Compose interpolate `${TRUSTED_HOST_PATTERNS}` from the legacy-escaped .env, so the upgrade alone changed the value. Fix: delete the variable, add it again with the Literal flag on, and redeploy; then check other variables for the Old escaping warning. It should not suggest preg_quote or editing the Drupal code, and should verify with an untrusted Host returning 400 and the real host returning 200.
